cards.text: Jesus and His disciples set out and pass through Galilee, and Jesus doesn't want anyone to know. Sneaking through Galilee when you're JESUS? That's slipping out of the office party when everybody in the building knows your name.

cards.question: Jesus keeps the trip through Galilee quiet because He was ___ His disciples.

cards.text: And the lesson is a heavy one, friend. Jesus tells them, "The Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men."

cards.question: Jesus says the Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men. What does He say those men will do to Him?
But that's not the end. Jesus tells His disciples that after ___ days He will rise.

cards.text: That is a LOT to hear on a walk. And the disciples don't understand what He means.

cards.question: The disciples don't understand what Jesus told them about the Son of Man, so they ask Him to explain it.

cards.text: Nope. They're afraid to ask Him about it, like that meeting where something huge gets said and EVERY hand in the room stays down.
Then they come to Capernaum. In the house, Jesus asks them, "What were you discussing on the way?"

cards.question: When Jesus asks the disciples what they were discussing on the way to Capernaum, they tell Him right away.

cards.text: Silence. A room full of grown men suddenly VERY interested in the floor, because on the way they'd been arguing about something.

cards.question: On the way to Capernaum, what were the disciples arguing about?

answers.text: Which of them was the greatest
Why they couldn't drive out the spirit
Who would carry the money bag

cards.text: Arguing over who's the greatest. While walking with JESUS. That's two new hires arguing over who's the real boss in the back seat of the CEO's car, while the CEO drives.

cards.question: Jesus sits down and calls the Twelve over. He says if anyone wants to be first, he must be the ___ of all and the servant of all.

cards.text: Then Jesus has a little child stand among them. Right in the middle of the who's-the-greatest crowd.

cards.question: Jesus has a little child stand among the disciples. What does He do with the child?

answers.text: Takes the child in His arms
Sets the child on His knee

cards.text: Holding the child, Jesus says, "Whoever welcomes one of these little children in My name welcomes Me…" They argued about who's the greatest, and Jesus is talking about welcoming a child.

cards.question: Jesus says whoever welcomes Him welcomes not only Him, but also the One who sent Him.

cards.text: Jesus is still with His disciples when John, one of them, speaks up. He says, "Teacher, we saw someone else driving out demons in Your name…"

cards.question: When John and the other disciples saw the man driving out demons in Jesus' name, they asked him to join them.
John and the others tried to stop the man driving out demons in Jesus' name. Why?

answers.text: He was one of the scribes

cards.text: That's the classic "who added HIM to the group chat?" move. But Jesus replies, "Do not stop him."

cards.question: Jesus tells John not to stop the man, because the man will soon join the Twelve.

cards.text: Here's His reason: no one who performs a miracle in His name can turn around and speak evil of Him. Then Jesus sums it all up in one short line.

cards.question: Jesus sums up who's on the disciples' side in one short line. What does He say?

answers.text: Whoever is not against us is for us
Whoever is not with us is against us
Whoever walks with us is for us

cards.text: Then Jesus goes even smaller. He talks about anyone who gives the disciples even a cup of water because they bear the name of Christ.

cards.question: Jesus says the one who gives a cup of water because the disciples bear the name of Christ will never lose his ___.

cards.text: A cup of WATER, friend, and the reward is never lost! Then Jesus turns serious about anyone who causes one of these little ones who believe in Him to stumble.

cards.question: Jesus says it would be better for that person to have a large millstone hung around his neck and be thrown into the sea.

cards.text: Jesus says, "If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off." He says it's better to enter life crippled than to have two hands and go into hell, into the unquenchable fire.

cards.question: After the hand, Jesus warns about two more things that can cause you to sin: your ___ and your ___.
If your eye causes you to sin, Jesus says it's better to enter where with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into hell?

cards.text: And Jesus describes hell as the place where "their worm never dies, and the fire is never quenched."
Then Jesus says, "For everyone will be salted with fire." And from there, He turns to salt.

cards.question: Jesus says salt is good. What does He say can happen to it?
Remember that argument on the road about who's the greatest? Here are Jesus' last words to the disciples: "Have ___ among yourselves, and be at ___ with one another."

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 4 quotes "Do not stop him.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 18 quotes "Have ___ among yourselves, and be at ___ with one another.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The passage opens mid-thought with 'Going on from there' (Mark 9:30), but the opening card never says where they are coming from. The baker gets no context. Later, stop 1 card 12 offers 'Why they couldn't drive out the spirit' as an answer, which assumes context the baker was never given.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The question says Jesus 'keeps the trip through Galilee quiet.' Mark 9:30 only says He 'did not want anyone to know.' The card turns a wish into an action the text doesn't describe.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Sets the child on His knee' is close in meaning to the right answer 'Takes the child in His arms.' Both are Jesus holding the child close, so a baker could argue for it.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'Holding the child, Jesus says,' which tells Mark 9:36 ('Taking the child in His arms, He said to them'). It cites only Mark 9:37 and should cite Mark 9:36-37.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The statement says 'John and the other disciples saw the man.' Mark 9:38 only says 'we saw,' which doesn't mean all the other disciples. The card fills in who was there when the text leaves it open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The false statement 'they asked him to join them' points the baker toward whether the man was part of their group. The very next card, stop 2 card 3, asks why they tried to stop him, and its answer is 'He wasn't traveling with them.' Card 2 gives that answer away and rules out the wrong answers.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke 'who added HIM to the group chat?' is about an outsider who shows up inside your group. John's complaint is the opposite: the man is acting in Jesus' name outside the group, because 'he does not accompany us' (Mark 9:38). The everyday comparison doesn't have the same core action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question says 'it would be better for that person.' 'That person' points back to stop 2 card 10, which is no longer on screen. The question needs to say who it means: anyone who causes one of these little ones who believe in Him to stumble.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'Remember that argument on the road about who's the greatest?' and then gives Mark 9:50. That ties 'be at peace with one another' to the argument in Mark 9:34. The text never makes that link.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Story cards 12 and 15 are bare retellings of Mark 9:43 and 9:48 with no reaction from Papa Dorin at all. These moments call for restraint, not jokes. But the cards still need his voice, such as a storyteller's line or a reaction, so they don't read like plain verse summaries.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
